report_summary.core_claims_joined:
LRIG1 and ERBB2 show co-enriched expression in malignant cells with validated coexpression support, nominating this pair as a prioritized follow-up axis for perturbation testing. Not yet established: whether LRIG1 modulation alters ERBB2 signaling output in breast cancer malignant cells.
CDH1 and ERBB3 exhibit malignant cell-intrinsic coexpression with enriched target-vs-rest signals, supporting ERBB3 as a perturbation-development follow-up candidate. Not yet established: whether CDH1 status predicts ERBB3 inhibitor response.
PTPRF and INSR show co-enriched expression in malignant cells, suggesting coordinated regulation worth evaluating as a cross-target follow-up. Not yet established: whether PTPRF modulates INSR signaling or drug sensitivity.
LAMA5 and BCAM exhibit malignant cell-intrinsic coexpression with enriched signals, nominating this ECM-receptor axis as an exploratory pathway for breast cancer malignant cell biology. Not yet established: whether LAMA5-BCAM interaction influences invasion or drug resistance.
NECTIN2 and NECTIN4 show malignant cell-intrinsic coexpression with enriched target-vs-rest signals, supporting evaluation of this nectin family pair as a co-observed target context. Not yet established: whether NECTIN2 modulates NECTIN4-directed therapeutic responses.
EFNB2 and EPHB4 are FEATURED genes with stage3 and OpenTargets evidence supporting gene-level follow-up; Stage 1 pair EFNB2--EPHB4 is coexpression-depleted in malignant cells and cited only as secondary spatial-niche framing context. Not yet established: whether EFNB2-EPHB4 signaling contributes to malignant cell phenotypes in breast cancer.

report_summary.core_claims_joined:
The EGF--ERBB2 pair shows interest-cell intrinsic support in malignant cells with strong coexpression enrichment (target_pct=0.024, risk_ratio=69.9) and ERBB2 expression enrichment (target_pct=0.37, risk_ratio=6.2). Stage 3 evidence confirms ERBB2 has extensive drug development history with 58 matched compounds including multiple breast cancer indications. Not yet established: whether EGF ligand availability limits ERBB2-driven proliferation in this context.
EPHB4 is a FEATURED high-priority validated target with 4 known drug programs including sorafenib with breast cancer indication at phase 3. The EFNB2--EPHB4 pair provides secondary spatial-niche framing only (coexpression depleted in malignant cells), so EPHB4 prioritization rests on gene-level actionability evidence rather than intrinsic pair mechanism. EFNB2 is covered by gene-level OpenTargets evidence. Not yet established: whether EPHB4 inhibition yields disease-relevant cellular readouts in breast cancer malignant cells.
The NECTIN2--NECTIN4 pair shows interest-cell intrinsic support with strong coexpression enrichment (target_pct=0.127, risk_ratio=53.3) and NECTIN4 expression enrichment (target_pct=0.247, risk_ratio=38.8). Stage 3 evidence identifies NECTIN4 as drug-targetable with matched compounds. Not yet established: whether NECTIN2-NECTIN4 homophilic/heterophilic interactions drive malignant cell adhesion phenotypes.
LAMA5 shows interest-cell intrinsic support through three separate passed pairs with receptor partners in malignant cells, each with enriched expression and coexpression. Stage 3 evidence shows no matched ChEMBL drugs for LAMA5; OpenTargets provides disease association support. The receptor partners provide co-expression context but lack independent Stage 3 drug support. Not yet established: whether LAMA5-mediated ECM remodeling drives malignant cell invasion or metastasis phenotypes.
The CDH1--ERBB3 pair shows interest-cell intrinsic support with CDH1 expression enrichment (target_pct=0.47, risk_ratio=4.7) and ERBB3 expression enrichment (target_pct=0.38, risk_ratio=4.3). Stage 3 evidence confirms ERBB3 has 22 matched drug programs including osimertinib. Not yet established: whether CDH1-ERBB3 coexpression reflects functional interaction or shared regulatory program.
The PTPRF--INSR pair shows interest-cell intrinsic support with PTPRF expression enrichment (target_pct=0.59, risk_ratio=5.6) and INSR expression enrichment (target_pct=0.34, risk_ratio=1.4). Stage 3 evidence confirms INSR has matched drug programs including BMS-754807 with breast cancer indication. Not yet established: whether PTPRF-INSR interaction modulates insulin signaling in malignant cells.
